title: The $2000 Draft Starts Now! | Arena Limited Championship Qualifier Draft 2 | Reality Fracture
event: Arena Limited Championship Qualifier (draft 2): live Arena pod with a pick timer, drafting for gems and, with five wins, $1,000 and qualification (6-1 or better $2,000); match format (best of one or three) not stated before the cut-off
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/GRW7THxCZuk (pack 14 cards at P1p1; pool-right layout only at P1p2, pool below from P1p3; pick start times from OCR (tesseract) of the Pack|Pick banner at 2 s and 1 s steps, P1p2 and P1p3 from the pool-right banner); takes from the transcript, the pool counter and the pick tag, checked against the final deck screen at 940 s; hover popups hid some cards; transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; cut-off 945 s

colour_path.quote: noting this doesn't necessarily lock us into red
We could still end up in like Sultai good stuff and abandon the red

colour_path.main: green-black self-mill, three or four colours
colour_path.quote: we might be delving into four colors here, folks

colour_path.main: green-black base, splash blue and red
colour_path.quote: Green black base splashing blue and red
I think we're just going to go full Sultai and just play a lot more Islands.

colour_path.main: green-black-blue ramp, red splash for Aerid Konstrari
colour_path.quote: this is what we drafted, so this is, you know, what we're going to do.

picks.reasoning: Violent Echoes: kills something and draws a card for four mana, and nothing else in the pack comes close; Samut and Vigorbloom Vanguard are the other options. It does not lock him into red.

considered.Samut, Hazoret's Champion: fine rare, not something he takes here

quotes: Violent Echoes is probably the pick here
Most of the time, you're going to kill something and then draw a card

picks.reasoning: Verdant Kraken: a legitimate bomb if you can ramp into it, so he builds towards it; he does not want to take Memory Trap after Violent Echoes. No Admittance would stay the course with red removal.

considered.Memory Trap: does not want to go Memory Trap after Violent Echoes
considered.No Admittance: very solid red removal, the other consideration

quotes: This card is a legitimate bomb. You just have to build around it.
I'm not going to have somebody just pass me a Verdant Kraken and not try to get there with this card.

picks.reasoning: Protege's Awakening over Way of the Wildspeaker: the better card and a perfectly fine splash; Vraska's Final Mercy and Compelled Brutality are not options for him.
quotes: Protege's Awakening is a better card
it's also a perfectly fine splashable

picks.reasoning: Primal Witchstalker is the best card in the pack; he takes the best card one pick at a time and may end Sultai and drop red. Wrath of the Bloodmane is a solid removal spell he passes.
picks.plan: Best card each pick; could be Sultai good stuff and abandon red.
quotes: We're just taking it one pick at a time. I'm just taking the best card.
We could still end up in like Sultai good stuff and abandon the red

picks.reasoning: Something Worth Saving over Archive Arbiter: with Witchstalker and this he is building towards a graveyard value strategy; he already has Kraken as a top end and is more likely to find large creatures later than value cards.

considered.Archive Arbiter: fine top-end card, but he already has Verdant Kraken
considered.Way of the Pyromancer: not good unless on the play

quotes: we are building towards some kind of graveyard-based value strategy, and I think that's a really good place to be

picks.reasoning: Vinelasher Adept: smooths draws (basic landcycling) and keeps the second colour open; he does not want to commit to black yet. Theoretical Necromancer and a second Arbiter were available.

considered.Theoretical Necromancer: pretty good, but he does not want to commit to black

picks.plan: Figure out the second colour later.
quotes: I don't necessarily want to commit to the black just yet. I think I'm going to take Vine Lasher Adept because it smooths out your draws
This way we can kind of figure out what our second color needs to be

picks.reasoning: Sureshot Sower as fine filler with something to play early.
quotes: It's fine filler level card, right? Just to, you know, have something to play early.

picks.reasoning: A weak pack with nothing he wants to play: he takes Fatehold Annex (the captions garble it) as a land for a splash he is looking to make.
quotes: this pack is quite weak. I don't really want to play any of these cards
That is a card that I'm looking to splash

picks.reasoning: Ferocity of the Hunt over Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign: he does not love either; he has good enters-the-battlefield effects to reuse, and notes he is not seeing a ton of red.
quotes: I don't really love Edgar. I don't really like Ferocity of the Hunt ... But maybe this is I do have some good come into play effects.
Noting that we're not seeing a ton of red.

picks.reasoning: Mabel, Bitter Recluse over Restore with Empathy: focus on the cheaper part of the curve.
quotes: Let's focus on the cheaper part of our mana curve here.

picks.reasoning: Void Extrapolator (self-mill); a Tome is in the pack, Ferocity of the Hunt wheels as a trick. Black seen late makes him feel okay about the spot.
quotes: certainly we are setting up for some self-mill stuff
seeing the late makes me feel okay about this spot

picks.reasoning: Not discussed; a three-card pack (Loot, the Anomaly; Predictive Preparations; Mountain). The take is not identified: the final deck screen does not show the sideboard.
Not discussed. Two cards left (Yargle, Glutton of Urborg and a Forest); the take is inferred from the last pick showing the Forest.
Last card, Auto Select.

Last Gasp over Plan for All Outcomes (fantastic, but he takes the safe cheap interaction): decks like this are often clunky and Last Gasp helps shore up a lot of things. Bestial Incursion and others are fine.
picks.plan: Take a good cheap interactive spell.
quotes: Play it safe. Take a good cheap interactive spell
often times when I draft these decks, I find that they can be a little clunky and Last Gasp really helps shore up a lot of things

picks.reasoning: Aerid Konstrari: a green-green-red 5/4 flyer that leaves a Heartwood token; very splashable power, and the reason he took Vinelasher Adept.
quotes: Yeah, this card is
this is why you take the Vine Lasher Adept, right? Because it gives you the opportunity to splash for busted cards like the Aerid Konstrari.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment: a premium uncommon for this self-mill deck, even if it pushes him towards four colours; Room of Refuge is a good fixer but this is the stronger card. He now has to respect his mana.

considered.Room of Refuge: good mana fixer, passed for the premium uncommon

quotes: we might be delving into four colors here, folks, cuz Recursive Recruitment seems awesome in this style of deck
now I'm going to need to respect my mana to some degree

picks.reasoning: Murmuring Volume over Theoretical Necromancer: it lets him cast all his cards and works with self-mill; with the power and ramp of the deck he calls it a Murmuring Volume deck.

considered.Theoretical Necromancer: good, but Murmuring Volume suits what the deck does

quotes: This lets us just cast all of our cards
this is actually a pretty good Murmuring Volume deck

picks.reasoning: Arcane Amphisbaena: a solid two-drop with deathtouch that surveils to fill the graveyard; he does not need more expensive cards like Archive Arbiter.

considered.Archive Arbiter: does not need more good expensive cards

quotes: I don't need good expensive cards like the Archive Arbiter. I will very happily take the Arcane Amphisbaena here as a solid two-drop.

picks.reasoning: Second Murmuring Volume: he commits to full ramp, green-black base splashing blue and red; Undulating Witness, Twinned Vision and Greenhouse Propagator are passed (Propagator worse than Volume for what the deck does).

considered.Greenhouse Propagator: worse than Murmuring Volume for this deck

picks.plan: Green-black base, splash blue and red.
quotes: Let's go full ramp.
Green black base splashing blue and red

picks.reasoning: Konstrari Improviser: a solid two-drop that ramps, one more way to get to Verdant Kraken.
quotes: solid two-drop that helps me ramp. Just more ways to try to get to that Verdant Kraken is nice.

picks.reasoning: Bestial Incursion: good with self-mill and gives late-game things to do; Keeper of the Quiet Hour is also fine, Theorix Metamage is okay.
quotes: Yes, really good with self-mill, gives you more late game things to do.

picks.reasoning: Theorix Annex (a dual land): he would like to pick up lands to support the splash cards and does not need another Way of the Wildspeaker.
quotes: at this point I would like to be able to pick up some lands to be able to support some of these cards
I would much rather have Theorix Annex here

picks.reasoning: Arni, Humble Scribe on the splash over Solve for Disappointment, which he never wants to play; he calls Arni on the splash kind of weak too. He is not main-decking Essence Burn (seen in the next pack).

considered.Essence Burn: not main-decking it, wonders about hate-drafting

quotes: I think I'll take Arni on the splash. I don't think I ever want to play Solve for Disappointment.

picks.reasoning: Shatterwing Pegasus taken (the slot empties at about 640 s) from Essence Burn, Sphinx's Approach, Plains; his stated thought is about hate-drafting Essence Burn, so the pick is a low-value take from a pack with nothing for him.

considered.Essence Burn: not main-decking; wonders if hate drafting is worth it

quotes: I'm not main decking Essence Burn.
Like I wonder if hate drafting even

picks.reasoning: Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun from Samut, Skilled Battlecarver, Island (take read from the card flying to the pool). Not discussed beyond needing interaction.
quotes: We do need some interaction. We'll be looking out for that here.

picks.reasoning: Academic Ascent from Academic Ascent and Forest. Not discussed.
Last card, Auto Select (Forest).
Paradox Shaper: nothing else in the pack for him (a bad pack to open); it self-mills every turn and goes with the graveyard cards. Keeper of the Quiet Hour was the other playable.
quotes: Wow, this pack is really bad for us.
I guess I'll take Paradox Shaper. Just being able to self-mill every single turn

picks.reasoning: Primal Witchstalker: premium. He would love a reanimation spell or removal but there is none.
quotes: Primal Witchstalker is so premium.
Would love a reanimation spell here. Would love removal.

picks.reasoning: Proft, Sinister Mastermind over Mind Meanderer: double blue is really hard for him; Proft is not great but acts as a trick and the deck gets threshold easily; there are few good options.

considered.Proft, Consulting Detective: blue card he does not want

quotes: double blue is really hard, right? So, I don't think I take it here.
I'm not super high on Proft, Sinister Mastermind, but there really isn't that many good options here.

picks.reasoning: The black-green dual land (Formidable Commons) over big creatures and Yoshimaru: his deck ramps into Krakens and wants mana; Tam's Resistance is decent.
quotes: I don't think I need big things or the Yoshimaru
our deck is trying to ramp into Krakens

picks.reasoning: Another Primal Witchstalker; Theoretical Necromancer would also be nice but the Witchstalker fits what the deck does.
quotes: Another Primal Witchstalker, okay.
Theoretical Necromancer would also be a nice pick up, but our deck is trying to ramp into Krakens

picks.reasoning: The blue-red dual land (Innovative Commons) with nothing else available; he thinks he can play Protege's Awakening for card draw and maybe Arni.
quotes: I'll take a blue red land with nothing else available.
I can probably play Protege's Awakening for like a little more card draw

picks.reasoning: Sureshot Sower from an empty pack; the green-white land is for white, the only colour he does not splash.

considered.Vigorbloom Annex: green-white land, white is the colour he does not splash

quotes: Empty pack. There's a green white land, but white is the only color we don't have to splash. I guess I'll just take a Sower.

picks.reasoning: Hapatra over Merfolk Skydiver (the captions): not a card he is interested in splashing, but nothing better; he has to play all these cards.

considered.Merfolk Skydiver: does not feel like a Skydiver deck

quotes: I guess I'll take Hapatra, but like not really a card that you're really interested in splashing.

picks.reasoning: Keeper of the Quiet Hour is fine; maybe he has to play it for some good late game. He wonders whether his pod just plays decks like this.
quotes: Keeper of the Quiet Hour is fine.
Maybe I have to play this for some good late game.

picks.reasoning: A land (Transformative Commons) while he says he needs interaction and another big late-game thing; he decides to go full Sultai and play more Islands, cutting two cards from the list.
quotes: I think we're just going to go full Sultai and just play a lot more Islands.
We did pick up the four dual lands, so I think it's more possible.

picks.reasoning: Mind Meanderer wheels from pick 3; read from the Pick tag, and it is in the final deck.
Afterthought Sentry from Tetsuko Umezawa, Rampart Hunter and the Sentry. Not discussed.
Living Library from Living Library and Mountain. Not discussed.
Last card, Auto Select (Charge the Sanctum).
